description: Masking, reads: every masked table a statement reads is replaced by a subquery projecting its columns through their masks, so filters, joins, groupings, aggregates, set operations and CTEs above it only ever see masked values. Views over masked tables, schema.table.column references, system columns, TABLESAMPLE and misfit transforms deny.

cases.name: a masked column is read through the masking subquery; every column of the table is projected, each through its own mask
cases.sql: SELECT email FROM users

expect.statement: SELECT email FROM ( SELECT id AS id, org_id AS org_id, '***'::text AS email, name AS name, pg_catalog.encode(pg_catalog.sha256(pg_catalog.convert_to(pg_catalog.textcat(pg_catalog.current_setting('midplane.mask_salt'), ssn), 'UTF8')), 'hex') AS ssn, CASE WHEN pg_catalog.length(phone) OPERATOR(pg_catalog.<=) 4 THEN pg_catalog.repeat('*', GREATEST(pg_catalog.length(phone), 1)) ELSE pg_catalog.textcat(pg_catalog.textcat(pg_catalog.left(phone, 0), pg_catalog.repeat('*', pg_catalog.length(phone) OPERATOR(pg_catalog.-) 4)), pg_catalog.right(phone, 4)) END AS phone, '***'::text AS bio, pg_catalog.floor(salary OPERATOR(pg_catalog./) 1000) OPERATOR(pg_catalog.*) 1000 AS salary, (pg_catalog.date_trunc('year', birthday))::date AS birthday, created_at AS created_at, CASE WHEN false THEN tags END AS tags FROM public.users ) AS users
